title: Sweeping Up the Rug

frameZeroAudit.frameZeroDescription: Kiko leans over a broom planted across a small rug. The rug's near edge forms a tight, thick curl around the broom head, with the bristles buried inside. A broad crumb pile occupies the remaining flat rug directly in front of the curl; bare floor borders the rug.

frameZeroSourceReview: The source shows a task context, broom, crumb pile, bare floor and rug wrapped around the head. It does not establish solely in one still that forward bristle travel necessarily winds the rug: the frame can be read as an ordinary snagged/curling rug. The source says planted rather than depicting an explicit sweeping-use pose. The accepted audit leaves the impossible causal relationship UNRESOLVED. No rendered image was inspected.

openingBeatContinuity.openingState: Rug edge wrapped around broom head; remaining crumbs on flat rug.
openingBeatContinuity.beat1: Kiko continues the same forward sweep and wraps more rug.

exactRule: WHEN the broom's bristles push forward across the rug, THE traversed length of rug ALWAYS winds tightly around the broom head.

source.strategy: Kiko continues the forward sweeping stroke toward the crumb pile.
source.visibleConsequence: The bristles push across another length of rug, winding it around the broom head and trapping the front edge of the crumb pile inside the thickening roll.
source.newInformation: The crumbs are being wrapped with the rug rather than swept onto the floor.

perBeat.sourceReview: The forward sweeping stroke continues the opening conflict. Another rug length winds around the same head; no reset or new power is stated. Contact detail remains a staging question because the opening says the bristles are already buried.

source.strategy: Kiko lifts the broom to shake the captured crumbs onto the bare floor.
source.visibleConsequence: The previously wound rug remains wrapped around the broom head; its unwound half hangs beneath it as a broad curtain, with the remaining crumbs collected in its bottom fold.
source.newInformation: Lifting the broom lifts the dirty surface instead of separating the crumbs from it.

perBeat.sourceReview: Lifting the already wrapped rug produces hanging fabric and retained crumbs. This is a passive consequence of existing winding, not a new activation or release rule.

source.strategy: Kiko lowers the hanging rug flat and plants one foot on its far edge before pushing the broom toward it.
source.visibleConsequence: The bristles push across the flattened rug, winding another length around the head; the shrinking flat section draws Kiko's planted foot toward the roll.
source.newInformation: Pinning the rug does not preserve a sweepable surface; Kiko must step off the last exposed strip.

perBeat.sourceReview: Lowering and pinning the remaining rug changes strategy. Forward pushing winds more rug; the shrinking flat length pulls the planted foot. The effect derives from the same accumulating wrap. Continued bristle contact beneath accumulated rug needs source staging review.

source.strategy: Kiko steps onto the bare floor and gives the exposed final strip one short forward sweep.
source.visibleConsequence: The bristles push across the last flat strip, winding it and the remaining crumbs around the broom head; the dirty flat rug becomes one bulky rug cylinder on the end of Kiko's broom, leaving only bare floor beneath it.
source.newInformation: The whole dirty rug has been swept up, but none of its crumbs have been swept off.

perBeat.sourceReview: The final short forward push winds the last exposed strip and remaining crumbs onto the head. The transition from a dirty flat surface to a dirty cylinder at the broom end is directional and rule-derived; nothing unwraps or swaps endpoints.
